findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: The new condition calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition in this change is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm.java, and no no-arg overload exists in the class hierarchy. The `services` module will not compile, so the whole PR (including all the new tests) cannot build or run. The intended call is presumably `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which is already non-null inside this branch.

findings.title: Re-auth skip is disabled for every user whenever passkeys are enabled in the realm
findings.body: The shortcut that skips the username form during re-authentication is now bypassed for any user as soon as passkeys are enabled for the realm, regardless of whether that particular user has a passkey. A password-only user re-authenticating with prompt=login in a passkey-enabled realm is now shown the username page and must submit it, where previously they were skipped. The only new UsernameForm re-auth test uses a passkey-only user, so this regression for password-only users is not covered. If the intent is to only show the form when the user can use a passkey, the condition should check the user's passkey credentials rather than only the realm flag.

findings.title: Negative webauthn-button check uses catch(Exception), so it can pass vacuously
findings.body: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` (and again around line 312), the absence of the webauthn form is checked with `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { }`. Any Exception thrown while looking up the element, such as a WebDriverException from a stale or not-yet-loaded page, is swallowed and the check passes without verifying anything. The same PR and file already use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` for this kind of check, which only accepts the expected exception.

findings.title: Unused import NoSuchElementException left behind
findings.body: The two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` uses were replaced by `MatcherAssert.assertThat(...)` in this PR, so the `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` import is now unused. This can fail a checkstyle or unused-import check in the build.

findings.title: Unused PasswordCredentialModel import added by this PR
findings.body: The import `org.keycloak.models.credential.PasswordCredentialModel` is added in this PR, but nothing in the file references it (the new tests only use string/nullValue checks). It should be removed to keep the build's unused-import checks clean.
